findings.reason: In 'If streaming music can be accomplished within the law', streaming is a gerund (the act of streaming music) and is the subject of the clause. The project rule is gerund = n., and a verb entry would need the dictionary form 'stream', not 'streaming'. The current headword and POS do not match each other or the way the word is used here.

va.why: The current text matches the file and there is a real defect: [7] is now the only entry in zh2 that puts an -ing headword with a 'v.' gloss. Last round changed adj. to v. but the headword change was never made. The proposed fix, n., is wrong. In 'streaming music can be accomplished', streaming takes the direct object 'music', so it is a verbal gerund, and a noun cannot take an object. Project practice lists such gerunds under the verb lemma with v. In this same file [6] has 'obtaining' → obtain v., s21 and s41 do the same with approaching and implementing, s42 already has 'stream v.', and last round's two reviewers rejected the 'gerund = n.' rule for this exact item. The correct fix is to change the headword to 'stream', keep 'streaming' as the highlight and keep the verb gloss.
va.amended_proposed: - stream  (单词)  v. 以流媒体方式播放（音乐、视频等）；流式传输   ← 高亮原文: "streaming"   [headword changes from 'streaming' to 'stream'; POS stays v.; the highlighted text stays "streaming"]

vb.why: The current entry contradicts itself: the headword is the -ing form 'streaming' but is labelled v. In 'If streaming music can be accomplished', streaming is a gerund (or an attributive noun) acting as the subject, not a finite verb. Every other -ing headword in the set is glossed as n. (shifting, licensing, bullying, safeguarding), so this change matches the project convention. The proposed 'n. 流媒体播放；流式传输（音乐、视频等）' is accurate and fits the ZH translation 流媒体音乐. It does not change the meaning.

findings.current: 这不过是说，我们能够观察到自己产生了某种渴望、某个快乐的念头，甚至某种可怕的情绪，而不在当下做出反应，进而放大这种感受，或让思绪一发不可收拾地陷入对往事的回想或对未来之事的预想。
findings.proposed: 这不过是说，我们能够观察到自己产生了某种渴望、某个快乐的念头，甚至某种可怕的情绪，而不会在当下做出放大这种感受的反应，也不会让思绪一发不可收拾地陷入对往事的回想或对未来之事的预想。
findings.reason: The scope of the negation is misleading. The English "without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling" rules out a specific kind of reaction: one that amplifies the feeling or sets the mind spiraling. In Chinese, "不A，进而B" naturally reads as "don't A, and as a result B", so "不在当下做出反应，进而放大这种感受" can be taken to mean that not reacting amplifies the feeling, which is the opposite of the author's point. The fix puts the amplifying and spiraling inside the negation.

The headword includes "to", but the highlight is only "makes it possible for", so the "to" of "to target" is not highlighted and the phrase is only partly highlighted. The highlight should be "makes it possible for … to", as the sibling entry "make it impossible for…to" in another file does. The gloss is also aligned with the headword's "…" placeholder and that sibling's style. The main fix is the highlight; the gloss change is secondary.

va.why: The current text matches the file. The English negates only one kind of reaction: one that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling. The current ZH '而不在当下做出反应，进而放大这种感受' rules out any reaction at all, and its negation scope is ambiguous: it can be read as 'not reacting amplifies the feeling'. The proposal '不会在当下做出放大这种感受的反应，也不会让思绪……' puts both results inside the negation and keeps every element (在当下, 放大感受, 一发不可收拾地陷入, 回想/预想). It is precise and natural Chinese.

The current text matches the file, but the gloss '使某人能够做' is already an accurate and standard gloss for 'make it possible for sb to do'. Changing it to '使……能够（做某事）' is only a style tweak. The real problem the proposal names is the highlight, not the gloss: the headword includes 'to' but the highlight is only 'makes it possible for'. A gloss-field change cannot fix that. If it is fixed, it should be a separate highlight correction to "makes it possible for … to", with the gloss left as is.

vb.why: The current line is imprecise. "不在当下做出反应，进而放大这种感受" denies reacting at all, so the English restriction "in a way that amplifies…" is lost. It also invites the reading "don't react, and thus amplify". The proposal puts the amplifying and the spiraling inside the negation, keeps the meaning, and reads naturally.

vb.amended_proposed: Highlight: "makes it possible for … to" (same format as s31's "makes it impossible for … to"). Gloss: 使……能够（做某事）
vb.why: The real error is the partial highlight. The headword includes "to" but the highlight stops at "for", so the "to" of "to target" is left out. Changing only the gloss would leave that error in place, so the highlight must be extended. The gloss change on its own is only a matter of taste, since "使某人能够做" is not wrong, but it does match the sibling entry's "……" style.
